books.section: Topic 7.7 1920s: Innovations in Communication and Technology

primary_sources: U.S. Census Bureau, Statistical Abstract, Table HS-41

stimulus.text:
Motor vehicles registered in the United States:

| Year | Motor vehicles registered |
| 1910 | 469,000 |
| 1920 | 9,239,000 |
| 1925 | 20,069,000 |
| 1930 | 26,750,000 |

Source: U.S. Census Bureau, Statistical Abstract of the United States, Table HS-41, “Transportation Indicators for Motor Vehicles and Airlines, 1900 to 2001.”
stimulus.source_note: Table from the U.S. Census Bureau, Statistical Abstract, Table HS-41.

options.misconception: Registrations rose every year in the table. Nothing fell by half.

options.misconception: Registrations rose from under half a million to nearly 27 million. They did not stay the same.

options.text: rose from under half a million to millions

rationales.A: Registrations rose every year in the table. Nothing fell by half.
rationales.B: Registrations rose from under half a million to nearly 27 million. They did not stay the same.
rationales.C: The table shows steady growth, with no fall. The sharp rise came between 1920 and 1925.
rationales.D: In 1910 there were 469,000 vehicles, and by 1930 there were 26,750,000. That is a rise from under half a million to tens of millions.
rationales.general:
1. Read the first row: 469,000 vehicles in 1910.
2. Read the last row: 26,750,000 vehicles in 1930.
3. Compare them: the number grew about fiftyfold in twenty years.
4. Note the pace: the sharpest jump came between 1920 and 1925, when registrations more than doubled.
Remember: in a table, compare the first and last rows first to set the size of the change.
